articles.title: LED Matrix
articles.summary: Dense grey-black pixel grid of tiny glowing dots, like an LED screen turned on but showing static. A neutral dark grey with a lively white-grey shimmer, like TV static or a salt-and-pepper print; no colour survives, so it reads as grey.
articles.what: Dense RGB LED pixel grid surface glowing with individual addressable light dots Up close: A very fine static of white and pale tinted dots, 2-3 px, on a charcoal-black field; at 2x some dots show faint pink, green and blue fringes. The dots form short slanted dashes and no clear grid or rows are visible. From a distance: A neutral dark grey with a lively white-grey shimmer, like TV static or a salt-and-pepper print; no colour survives, so it reads as grey. Measured spec (average): metal 80, roughness 70, coat 53. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, sides.
Mood: techy, clean, industrial.
Era: futuristic, modern.
Fits: gt / sports car, open wheel, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "LED Matrix" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: wide panels show the shimmer
Bumpers and spoiler: the techy grain suits them
Solid colour numbers with an outline read; thin or grey ones fade into the dots.
Large plain graphics: bold shapes on top of the static look crisp
Pairs well with: black, white, chrome, blue.
pitfalls: Not a visible RGB pixel grid: the dots are mostly white with faint colour fringes, and no rows or columns show
Not rainbow: it reads grey and white
Avoid: numbers get lost in the pixel grid, next to other busy patterns.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 80 (pearl-level metal), roughness 70 (satin gloss), clearcoat 53 (strong-to-medium clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: numbers get lost in the pixel grid, next to other busy patterns.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: large plain graphics: bold shapes on top of the static look crisp; thin white or colour pinstripes: sharp lines against the grain
Patterns to avoid: glitter or flake: same scale, just noise; other fine dot or weave patterns: mush
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat variation at low strength: calms the shimmer; leave sparkle alone: already maximum
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Magnesium Burn
articles.summary: Dark olive-brown base scattered with blinding white-hot flare spots and fine metal sparks, like burning magnesium. A dark khaki car with big white light blooms like flares or stars; the glows are the main read at distance and the dot halos turn into a hazy shimmer.
articles.what: Intense white magnesium flare burn with blinding brightness and hot-metal sparkle shower Up close: Dark olive-khaki ground with about eight blown-out white glows, 60-140 px, each ringed by a halo of tiny cream dots that thin out into the dark. A few short cream dashes, 6-10 px, scatter like sparks. Soft blurry glows, crisp small dots. From a distance: A dark khaki car with big white light blooms like flares or stars; the glows are the main read at distance and the dot halos turn into a hazy shimmer. Measured spec (average): metal 161, roughness 37, coat 121. Shine: gloss. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: hood, roof, hero panel.
Mood: fiery, industrial, aggressive.
Era: modern, timeless.
Fits: stock car, gt / sports car, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Magnesium Burn" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and sides: the glows need space to read
Avoid small trim
The white glows swallow white numbers; use black or dark numbers with a white outline, away from the glows.
Fine speckle: low strength, adds more spark dust
Pairs well with: matte black, gunmetal, chrome trim, burnt orange.
pitfalls: Not fire or orange: the render is white and olive, with no warm colour
Not a smooth gradient: the glow halos are made of tiny dots
Avoid: small numbers over the bright spots, next to other sparkle finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 161 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 37 (high gloss), clearcoat 121 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: small numbers over the bright spots, next to other sparkle finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: fine speckle: low strength, adds more spark dust; thin stripes: only as a separate band, they get lost in the glows
Patterns to avoid: other glow or glitter patterns: doubles up; dense patterns: bury the flares
Spec overlays that work: gloss clearcoat: makes the dark more glassy; micro-flake: adds extra glints near the glows
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
